newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight demand steady, north Brazil eyed.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight demand steady, north Brazil eyed.

text.p: Sugar freight business was mostly confined to regular routes by major trade houses on Tuesday, but shipbrokers said demand was picking up as western hemisphere producers such as north Brazil got underway with their harvests.
Fiji Sugar Marketing was rumoured to be close to fixing its recent order for 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Fiji to Japan at a rate near to $22, shipbrokers said.
Czarnikow Rionda fixed 19/21,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to Casablanca for mid-October at around $24.
South Africa Sugar Association (SASA) was said to have fixed 25,000 tonnes in bulk from Durban to Japan for September/October dates but details of the rate have yet to emerge.
New business included Booker with a 8/10,000-tonne bulk cargo from Georgetown to UK/Nantes, again for September/October.
Shipbrokers said Cargill was in the market for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to Morocco for 1/14 October as a replacement for an earlier large tonnage inquiry.
Lastly, E D & F Man quoted for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south China to Indonesia with Pakistan and Red Sea options for September/October dates.
Elsewhere, Brazil's Ministry of Industry and Commerce may raise as early as next week the sugar export limit exempted from tax, a senior commodities official said.
Pedro Cabral, head of the sugar and alcohol department, said studies were being completed to exempt from export tax the 20 percent of the sugar export quota which is not yet tax-free.
